function.mechanism: Used to control package headspace atmosphere and, in propellant uses, to expel product; EFSA describes packaging-gas and propellant technological functions.

adi.basis: EFSA 2025 re-evaluation concluded no safety concern and cites historical SCF position that ADI establishment for these atmospheric packaging gases/propellants is unnecessary.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA FAF concluded that use of oxygen (E948) as a food additive does not raise a safety concern; expected dietary exposure from additive use is very low.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR Part 184 (queried eCFR output showed no dedicated Oxygen food-additive section; oxygen matches in Title 21 query were non-food sections such as 21 CFR 868.5580)

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA oxygen entry queried did not provide a numerical ADI; EFSA reports JECFA set oxygen specifications at the 53rd meeting (1999) without a toxicological monograph.

concerns.summary: High-concentration inhalation oxygen toxicity (especially neonatal/high-FiO2 medical contexts) is biologically plausible, but EFSA indicates this is not representative of realistic food-additive exposure.
EFSA identified data gaps on manufacturing-process details and impurity coverage for E948 submissions, creating residual specification uncertainty.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2025 concluded E948 food-additive use does not raise a safety concern.
EFSA characterized E948 as low toxicological concern at intended food-additive use and very low expected dietary exposure.
No IARC classification entry was identified for oxygen/CAS 7782-44-7 in the current IARC classification dataset checked.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set; EFSA considered quantitative exposure estimation unnecessary for E948 in the 2025 re-evaluation because expected dietary exposure from additive use is low.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current regulatory evidence is strongly favorable for intended food-additive use: EFSA's 2025 review found no safety concern and very low dietary exposure relevance. Remaining uncertainty is primarily about manufacturing/impurity data completeness rather than demonstrated hazard at normal food-use exposure.
key_factors: No numerical ADI needed in EFSA/legacy SCF context
Very low expected dietary exposure from food-additive uses
No IARC listing found for oxygen
Residual impurity/manufacturing data gaps noted by EFSA
